allSaves.value: +1 status to all saves vs. magic

details.publicNotes:
In the unlikely event that a mortal manages to steal a vast amount of temporal essence from the Dimension of Time, all the while avoiding or defeating its guardians, upon death their soul might be cast to the Outer Rifts without stripping the stolen power. The eldritch influence of the Dimension of Time and the Outer Rifts' corruption coalesce into an oligtharu, a fate-rending fiend.

These esoteric demons represent the sin of rewriting history. They travel to mortal realms, where they build cults and seed lies to lay the groundwork for altering the past. They expect their followers to launder the reputations of heinous organizations while slandering virtuous groups, leading people astray on a massive scale.

An oligtharu rarely fights their own battles. When circumstances force these demons to fight directly, they use magic to tear their foes apart with brutal efficiency and bend reality in their favor.

Warping Reality

When deciding upon the limits of an oligtharu's temporal corruption, consider what would seem plausible to your players, what the demon would know, and how any other creatures involved in the temporal corruption would react to the situation. For example, an oligtharu who knows about one of the PC's old enemies might use fabricate truth on several PCs to convince them that the foe has just arrived on the scene. Since the foe did not fail a saving throw against fabricated truth, they'll likely be perplexed about why they've suddenly been transported in front of the PCs, and they might suspect the PCs of drawing them into a trap. Meanwhile, PCs who failed the save completely fall for the trick, PCs who critically succeeded know how reality was warped, and PCs who succeed at the save can decide what they believe happened according to the context around them. As long as at least one PC believes the trick, however, they'll have to contend with their old enemy!

Suggested Monster Parts

Monster Parts 10,000/24,000/45,000 gp

You temporarily stop time for everything but yourself, allowing you to use several actions in what appears to others to be no time at all. Immediately after casting freeze time, you can use up to 9 actions in 3 sets of up to 3 actions each.

After each set of actions, 1 round passes, but for only you, effects specifically targeting or affecting you, and effects that you create during the stoppage. All other creatures and objects are invulnerable to your attacks, and you can't target or affect them with anything.

Once you have finished your actions, time begins to flow again for the rest of the world. If you created an effect with a duration that extends beyond freeze time's duration, such as @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.IarZrgCeaiUqOuRu]{Wall of Fire}, it immediately affects others again, but it doesn't have any of the effects that happen only when you first Cast the Spell.

You surround yourself with supernatural splendor, appearing to be a god or similarly majestic being, with an appearance, regalia, and iconography of your choice. Targets must attempt a Will save. Regardless of the outcome, the target is then temporarily immune for 1 minute.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target must pay tribute to you two times. Paying tribute requires that the target spend a single action, which has either the move trait (as they bow) or manipulate trait (as they offer up a token in their hands). They must pay tribute at least once on each of their turns, if possible. While affected, the target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} by you and can't use hostile actions against you.

Failure As success, but the target must pay tribute a total of six times.

Critical Failure As failure, but the target must spend all its actions paying tribute, and they cannot take other actions until the tribute is fully paid.

You gain a sixth sense that warns you of danger that might befall the target of the spell. If you choose a creature other than yourself as the target, you create a psychic link through which you can inform the target of danger. This link is a mental effect. Due to the amount of information this spell requires you to process, you can't have more than one foresight spell in effect at a time. Casting foresight again ends the previous foresight. While foresight is in effect, the target gains a +2 status bonus to initiative rolls and isn't @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} against @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.VRSef5y1LmL2Hkjf]{Undetected} creatures or when flanked. In addition, you gain the following reaction: @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.VOEWhPQfN3lvHivK]{Foresight}

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spell-effects.Item.X9Na6IK8FSPcTuoc]{Spell Effect: Foresight}

You fill the targets' minds with endless images, like countless dreams and lives colliding with each other. The onrushing information deals @Damage[16d6[mental]] damage to each target, depending on its Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes half damage and can't use reactions until the start of your next turn.

Failure The target takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} until the start of your next turn.

Critical Failure The target takes double damage and is confused for 1 minute.

You howl a lament of damned souls. Each living enemy in the area takes 8d10 void damage and must attempt a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes full damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained} [[/r 1d4]].

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 4}.

You manifest a bubble of distorted time. The bubble is filled with tiny pockets where time runs slightly faster or slightly slower than normal. Movement through these temporal pockets is dangerous and disorienting, as muscles and bones slide out of sync with each other. Creatures that enter or begin their turn in the area must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} until it leaves the spell's area.

Failure The creature is clumsy 2 until it leaves the spell's area. While it remains in the area, whenever it uses a move or manipulate action, it takes 6d8 slashing damage with a basic Reflex save.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} until it leaves the spell's area.

Heightened (+1) The damage for using move or manipulate actions increases by 1d8.

Powerful wards hide a creature from magic that would spy on it or affect its mind. The target gains a +4 status bonus to saves against mental effects. Hidden mind attempts to counteract any detection, revelation, and scrying effects as if its spell rank were 1 higher than its actual rank. On a success, the effect functions normally except that it detects nothing about the target and its possessions. For instance, detect magic would still detect other magic in the area, but not any magic on the target.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-anachronism.spell-effects.Item.DBaMtFHRPEg1JeLs]{Spell Effect: Hidden Mind}

duration.value: until the next time you make your daily preparations

description.value:
You conjure a spectral scythe that gradually phases into reality above a target's head and follows them wherever they go. At the end of the creature's next three turns, an ominous bell tolls, and the creature must succeed at a Will save or be @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} on a critical failure); this effect has the emotion, fear, and mental traits. After the third toll, the scythe swings, striking the creature in the neck and dealing 10d10 slashing damage with a basic Fortitude save. If the spell reduces a target to 0 Hit Points, they die; this is a death effect.

Heightened (+1) Increase the damage by 2d10.

Magic empowers the target to act faster. It gains the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} condition and can use the extra action each round only for Strike and Stride actions.

Heightened (7th) You can target up to 6 creatures.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spell-effects.Item.ElkXovNrHB0Doi6O]{Spell Effect: Haste}

Requirements You have a planar key for the destination plane, used as a locus

You and your allies traverse the barriers between planes of existence. The targets move to another plane, such as the Plane of Fire, the Netherworld, or the Outer Rifts. You must know the destination plane exists and use a magic planar key created from material from that plane as a locus for the spell. While the planar keys for most prominent planes are uncommon, just like the spell interplanar teleport, more obscure planes and demiplanes often have rare or possibly even unique planar keys.

The spell is highly imprecise, and you appear 1d20×25 miles from the last place one of the targets (of your choice) was located the last time that target traveled to the plane. If it's the first time traveling to a particular plane for all targets, you appear at a random location on the plane. Interplanar teleport doesn't provide a means of return travel, though casting interplanar teleport again allows you to return to your previous plane unless there are extenuating circumstances.

You delve into the possible futures of the next few seconds to understand all the ways your foe might avoid harm, then cast out a vision of that future to those around you. Designate a creature. The first time each target makes an attack roll against that creature during true target's duration, the attacker rolls twice and uses the better result. The attacker also ignores circumstance penalties to the attack roll and any flat check required due to the designated creature being @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden}.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spell-effects.Item.HuvucQ5nfpuVWNrw]{Spell Effect: True Target}

duration.value: until the start of your next turn

description.value:
You scramble a creature's mental faculties and sensory input. The target must attempt a Will saving throw. Regardless of the result of that save, the target is then temporarily immune for 10 minutes. Warp mind's effects happen instantly, so @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} and other effects that counteract spells can't counteract them. However, @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.6dDtGIUerazSHIOu]{Wish} rituals and abilities that can remove non-magical effects can still counteract the effects.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target spends the first action on its next turn with the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} condition.

Failure The target is Confused for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The target is Confused permanently.

You magically spy on a creature of your choice. Scrying works like @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.zvKWclOZ7A53DObE]{Clairvoyance}, except that the image you receive is less precise, insufficient for teleport and similar spells. Instead of creating an eye in a set location within 500 feet, you instead create an eye that manifests just above the target. You can choose a target either by name or by touching one of its possessions or a piece of its body. If you haven't met the target in person, scrying's DC is 2 lower, and if you are unaware of the target's identity (perhaps because you found an unknown creature's fang at a crime scene), the DC is instead 10 lower.

The effect of scrying depends on the target's Will save.

Critical Success The spell fails and the target is temporarily immune for 1 week. The target also gains a glimpse of you and learns its rough distance and direction from you.

Success The spell fails and the target is temporarily immune for 1 day.

Failure The spell succeeds.

Critical Failure The spell succeeds, and the eye follows the target if it moves, traveling up to 60 feet per round.

You dilate the flow of time around the target, slowing its actions.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2} for 1 minute.

Heightened (6th) You can target up to 10 creatures.

You take command of the target, forcing it to obey your orders. If you issue an obviously self-destructive order, the target doesn't act until you issue a new order. The effect depends on its Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} as it fights off your commands.

Failure You control the target. It gains the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.9qGBRpbX9NEwtAAr]{Controlled} condition, but it can attempt a Will save at the end of each of its turns. On a success, the spell ends.

Critical Failure As a failure, but the target receives a new save only if you give it a new order that is against its nature, such as killing its allies.

Heightened (10th) The duration is unlimited.

description.value:
You cast your thoughts through a creature's mind, sifting for information. You access the target's memories and knowledge unless it fends you off with a Will save.

Success The target is unaffected.

Failure Each round of the spell's duration, you can Sustain the spell to ask a different question and attempt to uncover the answer. For each question, the target can attempt a Deception check against your spell DC; if the target succeeds, you don't learn the answer, and on a critical success, the target gives you a false answer that you believe is truthful Once you've asked the target a given question, asking it again, even with a separate casting of mind probe, produces the same result.

Critical Failure As failure, and the target takes a –4 circumstance penalty to Deception checks against your questions.

You instantly transport yourself and any items you're wearing and holding from your current space to an unoccupied space within range you can see. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you're carrying it in an extradimensional container—the spell is lost.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 1 mile. You don't need to be able to see your destination, as long as you have been there in the past and know its relative location and distance from you. You are then temporarily immune for 1 hour.

You alter the target's memories by erasing a memory, enhancing a memory's clarity, altering a memory, or adding a false memory. The target can attempt a Will save to resist the spell.

Critical Success The target is unaffected and realizes you tried to alter its memory.

Success The target is unaffected but thinks your spell was something harmless instead of rewrite memory, unless it identifies the spell.

Failure During the first 5 minutes of the spell's duration, you can Sustain the spell to modify a memory once each round. When you do, you imagine up to 6 seconds of memory to modify, to a maximum of 5 continuous minutes of memory.

Any memories you've altered remain changed as long as the spell is active. If the target moves out of range before the 5 minutes is up, you can't alter any further memories.

Heightened (6th) You can Cast the Spell on a willing target to suppress all memory of a particular topic, detailed in 50 words or fewer. The effect is permanent, and it patches these omissions with an indistinct haze.

Magic empowers the target to act faster. It gains the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} condition and can use the extra action each round only for Strike and Stride actions.

Heightened (7th) You can target up to 6 creatures.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spell-effects.Item.ElkXovNrHB0Doi6O]{Spell Effect: Haste}

You dilate the flow of time around the target, slowing its actions.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2} for 1 minute.

Heightened (6th) You can target up to 10 creatures.

You gain a vague glimpse of the future. During the casting of this spell, ask about the results of a particular course of action. The spell can predict results up to 30 minutes into the future and reveal the GM's best guess among the following outcomes: good, bad, mixed (the results will be a mix of good and bad), and nothing (there won't be particularly good or bad results).

The GM rolls a secret @Check[flat|dc:6|showDC:all|traits:secret]. On a failure, the result is always "nothing." This makes it impossible to tell whether a "nothing" result is accurate. If anyone asks about the same topic as the first casting of augury during an additional casting, the GM uses the secret roll result from the first casting. If circumstances change, though, it's possible to get a different result.

You see things within 60 feet as they actually are. The GM rolls a secret counteract check against any illusion, morph or polymorph effect in the area, but only for the purpose of determining whether you see through it (for instance, if the check succeeds against a polymorph spell, you can see the creature's true form, but you don't end the polymorph spell).

description.value: When a reaction would disrupt an oligtharu's spell, the demon can attempt a @Check[flat|dc:15], avoiding the disruption on a success.

Frequency once per day

Effect The oligtharu casts @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.6s0UW4bujggma9TC]. If at least one creature fails the save, the fabrication is consistent with that creature's knowledge of the world, and the oligtharu imagines a plausible chain of past events to justify the fabrication, the oligtharu can alter the timestream to turn the fabrication into the truth. The change persists as long as at least one creature believes it, after which point any created objects or creatures are destroyed and any transported objects or creatures are returned to their original locations. All creatures except those that failed the save against fabricated truth remember the original timestream and might notice discrepancies; creatures that critically succeeded automatically recognize what happened. This effect can't introduce hazards or creatures of 20th level or higher.

Saving Throw @Check[will|dc:41]

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (1 round)

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} (1 round)

Stage 3 @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} and sickened 2 (1 round)

Stage 4 confused, sickened 2, and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} (1 round)

Stage 5 As stage 4, but the victim is also under the effects of the flicker spell (1 round)

Stage 6 death. The creature's body and soul are dragged into and lost in the Dimension of Time.

The oligtharu can take on the appearance of any Small or Medium humanoid. This doesn't change their Speed or their attack and damage modifiers with their Strikes, but it might change the damage type their Strikes deal (typically to bludgeoning).

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]

Righting the oligtharu's impositions on memory and time brings the demon intense mental anguish. Whenever the oligtharu's @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.6s0UW4bujggma9TC] or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.FhOaQDTSnsY7tiam] is counteracted, the oligtharu takes @Damage[(3d10+14)[mental]] damage.
